issues.title: Prompt Drop #1: 10 copy-paste AI prompts people shared this week
issues.intro: Ten prompts people were actually sharing on X this week (Oct 8 to 15, 2026). Each one is beginner-friendly: copy it, swap the [brackets] for your own details, paste it into the AI tool, done.

prompts.title: Make the AI interview you first
prompts.prompt:
Before you answer, ask me 3 questions that would make your answer better. Wait for my replies.

[Your question or task]
prompts.why: The AI stops guessing about your situation and fills in the missing context before it writes anything.
prompts.author: @MaveStorm

prompts.title: A personal AI tutor for any topic
prompts.prompt: Act as my AI tutor. I want to learn about [TOPIC]. First, find out what I already know by asking me two questions. Then teach me one concept at a time using simple explanations and practical examples. Don't move to the next concept until I've understood the current one.
prompts.why: It sets the pace to your level and checks you understand before moving on, the way a good teacher would.
prompts.author: @Only_bigmel_
prompts.note: The last sentence was cut off in the original post, so we completed it.

prompts.title: A thinking partner that won't just agree with you
prompts.prompt:
Act as my critical thinking partner. Whenever I share an idea, identify my assumptions, challenge my reasoning, point out potential risks, and offer alternative perspectives. Don't agree with me just to be polite.

My idea: [your idea]
prompts.why: AI chatbots tend to agree with you. This tells it to push back, which is what you actually need before a big decision.
prompts.author: @YourGuyRye27

prompts.title: Roast my landing page (Hormozi's Value Equation)
prompts.prompt:
Use Alex Hormozi's Value Equation to roast my landing page. Find what's stopping visitors from buying and give me a prioritized plan to fix it.

[Paste your landing page URL or copy]
prompts.why: A named framework gives the AI a clear scoring lens, so you get specific fixes instead of vague "make it pop" feedback.
prompts.author: @OmriBuilds

prompts.title: Check how AI chatbots see your category
prompts.prompt: I'm looking for a [category] for [use case]. Which 5 options would you consider and why? Cite your sources.
prompts.why: Run it about 5 times. The sources the AI keeps citing are the sites you need to be listed on to show up in AI answers.
prompts.author: @finalcall000

prompts.title: Turn a messy brain dump into a to-do list
prompts.prompt:
Sort this into: 1) Do now (under 15 min), 2) Schedule, 3) Delegate, 4) Delete. For #1, give the first tiny step for each.

[Paste your brain dump]
prompts.why: The four buckets force a decision on every item, and the "tiny first step" makes it easy to start.
prompts.author: @NeyronixAI

prompts.title: Understand any confusing document
prompts.prompt:
Explain this like I'm smart but new: 1) a plain-English summary in 5 lines, 2) key terms defined, 3) what I must do next. Quote the exact lines you used.

[Paste the contract, policy or manual]
prompts.why: Asking for exact quotes lets you check the AI didn't make anything up. Great for contracts, policies and manuals.
prompts.author: @NeyronixAI

prompts.title: Build a simple app with no coding
prompts.prompt: Make one self-contained HTML task planner. Include fields for task, due date, and priority. Sort by due date, let me mark tasks complete, and save tasks in this browser. Use plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No libraries or server.
prompts.why: "One self-contained HTML file" means you can save the answer as planner.html and open it in your browser. Swap "task planner" for anything.
prompts.author: @AkhilPaladugu27

prompts.title: Stop the AI from over-engineering your code
prompts.tool: Claude Code, Cursor or any coding AI
prompts.prompt:
[Describe the feature you want]

Scoring: 1 point for each line of code you add. 2 points for each line you remove. Aim for the highest score.
prompts.why: Coding AIs love adding extra code. A simple scoring rule nudges them toward smaller, cleaner changes.
prompts.author: @vgnshiyer

prompts.title: The "caricature of me and my job" trend
prompts.prompt: Create a caricature of me and my job based on everything you know about me.
prompts.why: Upload a photo first. It works best if ChatGPT's memory is on, because it uses what it already knows about you. A fun first image prompt.
prompts.author: @j8vijfvkftmyjw
